Box cavity, all-wall — this is a pure blockMesh job; the two zones come from `topoSet` boxToCell → cellZoneSet. All key coordinates (10/30/70/90, 20/40, 4/24/16/36 mm) are multiples of 4 mm, so a coarse 4 mm mesh already resolves the zones exactly.

```python
import os, subprocess, textwrap
for d in ["system","constant/polyMesh","constant/triSurface"]: os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

head = """FoamFile{ version 2.0; format ascii; class dictionary; object %s; }\n"""

open("system/controlDict","w").write(head%"controlDict"+
"application blockMesh; startFrom startTime; startTime 0; stopAt endTime; endTime 1;\n"
"deltaT 1; writeControl timeStep; writeInterval 1;\n")
open("system/fvSchemes","w").write(head%"fvSchemes"+"ddtSchemes{default steadyState;} gradSchemes{default Gauss linear;} divSchemes{default none;} laplacianSchemes{default Gauss linear corrected;} interpolationSchemes{default linear;} snGradSchemes{default corrected;}\n")
open("system/fvSolution","w").write(head%"fvSolution"+"solvers{} \n")
print(sorted(os.listdir(".")))
```
Now the blockMeshDict, in metres, with each of the six walls named explicitly on the faces as they are written (no bbox guessing).
Zones via `topoSet`: heater 20 mm cube 4 mm above the floor at the x-min end, cooler the same 4 mm below the ceiling at the x-max end, both centred in y.

133/129 instead of 125: the x-faces of the boxes land exactly on cell centres. Shrink the *query* box by a quarter cell (the zone geometry is unchanged) so selection is unambiguous, and verify the resulting zone bounding boxes.
4×5×5 — the 10 mm inset puts the cube's x-faces mid-cell. Move the inset to 12 mm (heater 12–32 mm, cooler 68–88 mm, still symmetric about the cavity centre) so the cube lands on cell faces.
Coarse shape is right (125 cells = 5³ per zone). Refine to 2 mm cells and rebuild both mesh and zones, then measure.
1000 = 10³ cells per zone. Now measure the zones' actual bounding boxes from the mesh itself and render.
Zones aren't exposed by the reader, so parse `cellZones` labels directly and index the mesh cell centres (same ordering) to measure each zone's extent.
Numbers match the request. A picture to confirm placement (heater low at the x-min end, cooler high at the x-max end), then `checkMesh`.
The iso view's axis orientation is ambiguous; take a straight x–z side view to confirm heater is low and cooler is high.
Heater low at the near end, cooler high at the far end. Run `checkMesh`.

`checkMesh` clean; zone volumes 8e-06 m³ each = exactly 20 mm cubes, total volume 2.4e-04 m³ = 100×60×40 mm.

**Built:** a single hex block cavity, 0.100 × 0.060 × 0.040 m (metres, `scale 1`), 50×30×20 = 30 000 uniform 2 mm cells, meshed with `blockMesh` (no STL/snappy — the geometry is a box, so a surface mesh would only add error). All six boundaries are `type wall`, named on the faces as written: `floor`, `ceiling`, `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax`. No inlet/outlet exists.

**Measured against the request:** cavity bbox (0 0 0)–(0.1 0.06 0.04) m ✓; `heater` zone 1000 cells, bbox (12, 20, 4)–(32, 40, 24) mm = 20×20×20 mm, sitting 4 mm above the floor at the x-min end ✓; `cooler` zone 1000 cells, bbox (68, 20, 16)–(88, 40, 36) mm = 20×20×20 mm, 4 mm below the ceiling at the x-max end ✓. Both confirmed visually in the x–z view.

**My assumptions** (the request gave only the cavity size, the 20 mm cube size, and "near the floor / near the ceiling at the other end"): 4 mm clearance from floor and ceiling; 12 mm inset from the end walls (chosen so the cube faces land on cell faces — 10 mm put them mid-cell and gave a 4-cell-wide zone); cubes centred in y (20–40 mm); z taken as vertical; 2 mm uniform cell size.

**Not checked:** nothing thermal or physical — no fields, no boundary conditions, no gravity direction set anywhere in the case; the zones are cellZones only, with no material or source attached. No near-wall grading for the natural-convection boundary layer was added, so the 2 mm uniform spacing may need refinement depending on your Rayleigh number.
